questions.q: Per this lesson, what problem do enterprise architecture frameworks exist to solve?
options: They exist purely to generate paperwork required for compliance audits
They exist only to assign blame after an architecture failure occurs
They prevent an architecture effort from accidentally skipping an important category, like security or operability, while focused on the exciting problem in front of it
They are required by law for any company using Salesforce
questions.explain: Frameworks give architects a structured checklist of categories to work through specifically so that something important doesn't get skipped by accident while attention is focused on one exciting technical problem.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the Zachman Framework's structure?
options: A single linear checklist with no categorization
A matrix classifying artifacts along two axes: different perspectives (planner, owner, designer, builder) and different questions (what, how, where, who, when, why)
A Salesforce-specific tool available only inside Setup
A framework that applies exclusively to network security design
questions.explain: The lesson describes the Zachman Framework as a matrix-style framework crossing different perspectives against different questions, producing a structured way to ensure every perspective has considered every question.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are the five pillars of Salesforce's current Well-Architected framework?
options: Trusted, Easy, Adaptable, Fast, Cheap
Security, Scalability, Usability, Portability, Maintainability
Business, Data, Application, Technology, Governance
Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, Resource and Cost Optimization, Fairness
questions.explain: The lesson states Salesforce's current Well-Architected framework is organized around five pillars: Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, Resource and Cost Optimization, and Fairness, revised from an earlier three-quality version (Trusted, Easy, Adaptable).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Salesforce frames the five Well-Architected pillars as being in tension with one another?
options: Because only one pillar can ever be addressed in a single solution
Because increasing one quality, like reliability, may require more resources or add complexity that affects other pillars, forcing an explicit trade-off conversation
Because the pillars contradict each other and cannot coexist under any circumstances
Because Salesforce recommends ignoring four of the five pillars in every design
questions.explain: The lesson explains that Salesforce deliberately frames the pillars as being in tension -- for example, more reliability may cost more resources -- so the framework's value is surfacing that trade-off explicitly, not pretending every pillar can be maximized at once.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is the right way to use TOGAF, Zachman, or Well-Architected?
options: As a rigid sequence of steps an architect is graded on following exactly
As a tool that only applies during a formal, multi-month TOGAF engagement
As a replacement for understanding the business requirements of a project
As a completeness check against your own architecture work, asking 'did we actually think about this' category by category
questions.explain: The lesson's explicit guidance is to use any of these frameworks as a completeness checklist -- asking whether each category or pillar was actually considered -- rather than as a rulebook requiring full procedural ceremony.
